newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end lower, correction may continue.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end lower, correction may continue.

text.p: 1545 GMT - Swiss shares ended slightly lower in a consolidation of recent gains while market interest focused on UBS and on the expiry of options and futures.

Traders said derivatives-linked transactions underpinned the market but could not offset overall bearish sentiment. "We seem to be in for a bigger correction," one dealer said, citing the technically overbought situation and insecurity about the further direction of the U.S. dollar and Wall Street. He also said investors would be cautious ahead of U.S. Fed chairman Greenspan's testimony to the Senate Banking Committee next week. * Blue-chip SMI down 0.18 percent, or 8.3 points, to 4,522.5.
* All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) lost 4.01 points, or 0.14 percent, to end at 2,871.18.
Volume was moderate for an options and futures expiry day, one dealer said.

* UBS bearers ended up two francs at 1,298 after volatile trade. The bank reported a 1996 group net loss of 348 million francs due to previously announced one-off provisions, which according to dealers was more or less in line with expectations. One trader said he was pleased by the statement of UBS chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta who said he would be disappointed if the 1997 profits were below two billion francs.
Other financials were mixed with CS Group, SBC and insurer Zurich giving up ground. Swiss Re jumped 16 francs, or 1.06 percent, to 1,520.
* Novartis registereds added one franc to 1,792, while Novartis bearers fell three francs to 1,789. Roche was down 65 francs to 12,735. Clariant eased four to 714.
* Stocks of SMH and Sulzer fell around one percent each.
* The expiry of February contracts was smooth on the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex), dealers said.

166,279 options with a call/put ratio of 1.94 to one were traded. Activity was high in Nestle options with 27,206 calls and 4,563 puts and UBS with 26,670 calls and 9,315 puts. In UBS, volume was boosted by the release of the bank's 1996 figures and the fact that UBS traded around 1,300 francs on the cash market, which corresponded to a strike price.
Im SMI futures, 9,058 contracts changed hands. February SMI futures were quoted at 4,507.5 at the expiration.
